## Purpose
Defines what can be granted (the permissions), the five built-in roles, and the deny-by-default route policy that maps each `/api` route to the access it needs. The browser receives the same rules so it can hide what the caller cannot do.

## Responsibilities
- **`Permission(key, group, label, description, shared=False)`.**
- **`PERMISSIONS`, 26 keys:**
  - orchestrator.use, chat.use;
  - agents.view/manage, tools.view/manage;
  - workflows.view/run/manage/deploy;
  - connectors.view/manage, remote_servers.view/manage;
  - knowledge.view/manage;
  - catalog.view/manage (shared);
  - rules.view/manage (shared);
  - reviews.view/decide, logs.view;
  - vault.view/manage/reveal;
  - settings.view (shared).
- **`PERMISSION_KEYS` and `BY_KEY`.**
- **`SystemRole` and `SYSTEM_ROLES`:**
  - `maintainer`: every permission;
  - `builder`: every `.view`, plus orchestrator.use, chat.use, agents.manage, tools.manage, workflows.run, workflows.manage, connectors.manage, knowledge.manage and vault.manage;
  - `operator`: every view, plus chat.use and workflows.run;
  - `reviewer`: every view, plus reviews.decide;
  - `viewer`: every view.
- **`clean_permissions(values)`** returns the known keys only, sorted, without duplicates.
- **Access levels:** `PUBLIC`, `USER`, `ANY`, `ADMIN`, `SELF`, or `"perm"`.
- **`Rule(methods, pattern, access, perms, admin_ok)`.** It is built by `_r(methods, pattern, access="perm", *perms, admin_ok)`, where `"*"` means GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE and `"A|B"` lists methods. Patterns are anchored `^…$` and matched against the path without `/api`.
- **`RULES`, first match wins:**
  - `/auth/.*` → SELF; `POST /admin/auth/login` → PUBLIC; `/admin/.*` → ADMIN.
  - `GET /settings/public` → PUBLIC; `GET /settings/models/catalog` → ANY; `GET /settings` → settings.view, with admin_ok; any other `/settings` method → ADMIN.
  - `GET /status` and `GET /ops/<id>/events` → ANY.
  - `POST /orchestrate(/stream)?` → orchestrator.use or chat.use.
  - Chat completions and stream, conversations, and uploads (image, file, support) → chat.use or orchestrator.use.
  - `/runs/agent-evaluate` → agents.manage; `/runs/agent` → orchestrator.use; workflow-plan, workflow-refine and workflow-verify → workflows.manage; `/runs/rebuild` → workflows.manage or tools.manage; `/runs/synthesis` → tools.manage.
  - `GET /runs…` and `POST /runs/<id>/cancel|decisions…` → USER.
  - Agents, tools, `/mcp/` and connectors: GET needs `.view`; writes need `.manage` (connectors.* covers mcp).
  - Workflow executions: GET needs view, POST needs run.
  - `/workflows/<n>/execute` and `/inputs/` → run; `publish|register|export` and `/deployment/` → deploy; any other GET → view; any other write → manage.
  - Ontology: writes to annotations or classify accept any of agents, tools, workflows or catalog manage; other GETs need catalog.view; other writes need catalog.manage.
  - Processes: recommendations need knowledge.manage; `validate` and `templates/preview` need catalog.view; GET needs catalog.view; writes need catalog.manage.
  - Knowledge, rag and libraries: retrieve, search, graph/query and optimizer/preview, and every GET, need knowledge.view; writes need knowledge.manage.
  - Rules: `PUT /rules/agents/<id>` needs rules.manage or agents.manage; `/rules/suggest` accepts rules, agents or workflows manage; GET needs rules.view; writes need rules.manage. The same applies to `/safety-rules`.
  - Reviews: GET needs view; `POST /reviews/<id>/decision` needs decide.
  - `GET /observability…` needs logs.view.
  - Remote servers: GET needs view; writes need manage.
  - Vault: `rotate-key` and `generate-key` → ADMIN; reveal needs vault.reveal; GET accepts vault.view, vault.manage, workflows.manage or tools.manage; writes need vault.manage.
- **`export_rules()`** returns the rules as JSON for the browser: methods (sorted), pattern, access, perms, admin_ok.
- **`match(method, path)`** returns the first matching rule, or None, meaning deny.

## Interactions
- Used by `auth/middleware.py`.
- Used by `auth/store.ensure_system_roles`, which syncs the built-in roles to the database.
- `export_rules` is served to the frontend, which evaluates the same rules in JavaScript.

## Error handling and edge cases
An unmatched route is denied.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **Order matters:**
  - `/workflows/executions` must come before `/workflows/<name>`;
  - specific settings rules come before the `/settings` catch-all;
  - ontology tagging comes before the catalog catch-all.
- **Patterns use only regex syntax that JavaScript's `RegExp` reads the same way.**
- **Platform administration is not a permission.** Only admins can manage workspaces, users, roles, Settings writes, the vault master key and cleanup.

## How to rebuild this file
Copy the permission list, the roles and the rule list exactly, in this order. The exact bundle carries the text verbatim.
